body.statement:
For every law in \(\mathcal M(T,p,\mathcal S,\epsilon)\), the reshaped fixed-effect coefficient satisfies
\[
 \theta(\Pi)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{\ell=0}^{p}L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi)\tau_{t,\ell}.
\]
For arbitrary finite binary-path support, and \(j,r,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\),
\[
 G_{jr}(\Pi)=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-r)
 -T^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{v=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(t-j,v-r),
\]
\[
 h_{t,\ell,j}(\Pi)=T^{-1}\left\{C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-\ell)
 -T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^{T}C_{\Pi}(v-j,t-\ell)\right\},
 \qquad
 \sum_{t=1}^{T}L_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing, then \(C_{\Pi}(u,v)=K_{\Pi}(u,v)\) on every argument used above, so the same two displays hold with \(K_{\Pi}\) in place of \(C_{\Pi}\).
body.proof_tex:
Path overlap gives \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}>0\), so the inverse propensities in \(\theta(\Pi)\) are well defined.  Conditional on \(X\), consistency and conditional pathwise mean random assignment give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\left.\frac{\Pi_W}{\pi_W(X)}A_W(\Pi)Y\right|X\right]
 &=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\pi_s(X)\frac{\Pi_s}{\pi_s(X)}A_s(\Pi)
   \mathbb E_P[Y\mid W=s,X]\\
 &=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\Pi_sA_s(\Pi)\mu(s,X).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Let \(m(X)=(m_1(X),\ldots,m_T(X))^{\top}\).  The calendar-memory condition is
\[
 \mu(s,X)=m(X)+\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{\ell=0}^p
 e_t\tau_{t,\ell}(X)(D_s)_{t,\ell}.
\]
Since \(M(\Pi)=\sum_s\Pi_sD_s\),
\[
 \sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)=J\left(\sum_s\Pi_sD_s-M(\Pi)\right)=0.
\]
It follows that the unrestricted baseline cancels:
\[
 \sum_s\Pi_sA_s(\Pi)m(X)
 =T^{-1}G(\Pi)^{-1}\left(\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}\right)m(X)=0.
\]
For each effect cell,
\[
 \sum_s\Pi_sA_s(\Pi)e_t(D_s)_{t,\ell}
 =G(\Pi)^{-1}\left\{T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}e_t(D_s)_{t,\ell}\right\}
 =L_{\cdot,t,\ell}(\Pi).
\]
Taking expectation over \(X\), interchanging only finite sums, and using \(\tau_{t,\ell}=\mathbb E_P[\tau_{t,\ell}(X)]\) proves the causal loading representation.  The inverse exists by \(G(\Pi)\succ0\).

For the design identities, let \(W^{\Pi}\sim\Pi\), extend its coordinates by zero outside the panel, and note
\[
 M(\Pi)_{t,j}=\mathbb E_{\Pi}[W^{\Pi}_{t-j}],
 \qquad
 C_{\Pi}(u,v)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\Pi}(W^{\Pi}_u,W^{\Pi}_v).
\]
Using \(J_{uv}=\mathbf 1\{u=v\}-T^{-1}\) and expanding the definition of \(G\) coordinatewise gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G_{jr}(\Pi)
 &=T^{-1}\sum_{u=1}^T\sum_{v=1}^TJ_{uv}
   C_{\Pi}(u-j,v-r)\\
 &=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^TC_{\Pi}(t-j,t-r)
   -T^{-2}\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{v=1}^TC_{\Pi}(t-j,v-r).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Likewise,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 h_{t,\ell,j}(\Pi)
 &=T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^TJ_{vt}C_{\Pi}(v-j,t-\ell)\\
 &=T^{-1}\left\{C_{\Pi}(t-j,t-\ell)
  -T^{-1}\sum_{v=1}^TC_{\Pi}(v-j,t-\ell)\right\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
These calculations use no ordering or absorption.

If \(\mathcal S\) is absorbing, then for \(u\leq T\),
\[
 W^{\Pi}_u=\mathbf 1\{a(W^{\Pi})\leq u\}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 C_{\Pi}(u,v)
 =F_{\Pi}(\min\{u,v\})-F_{\Pi}(u)F_{\Pi}(v)
 =K_{\Pi}(u,v),
\]
including nonpositive boundary indices because both variables and \(F_{\Pi}\) are then zero.  This proves the ordered Green corollary.

Finally, with \(e_{\ell}\in\mathbb R^d\) denoting the lag-coordinate vector,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{t=1}^Th_{t,\ell}(\Pi)
 &=T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}D_se_{\ell}\\
 &=T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}\{D_s-M(\Pi)\}e_{\ell}\\
 &=T^{-1}\sum_s\Pi_sR_s(\Pi)^{\top}R_s(\Pi)e_{\ell}
 =G(\Pi)e_{\ell}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The second equality uses \(\sum_s\Pi_sR_s=0\); the third uses \(R_s=J(D_s-M)\), symmetry, and idempotence of \(J\).  Multiplication by \(G(\Pi)^{-1}\) gives
\[
 \sum_{t=1}^TL_{j,t,\ell}(\Pi)=e_j^{\top}e_{\ell}=\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}.
\]
body.justification: This is the exact causal coefficient map for arbitrary finite path supports, with the ordered Green kernel correctly restricted to absorption.
body.gap: The closest published RIPW result gives only homogeneous lag coefficients and does not display calendar-by-lag loadings.
body.consumer: The OpenTable analysis can report which calendar dates and causal lags contribute to each fitted coefficient.
